issue: Content format drives most of the reach difference
observation: X Article posts reach 1.91x the median views of the account's other authored posts (n=105, 90% CI 1.55-2.63). Lower formats: short_post 0.18x (n=10), long_post 0.53x (n=45).
algo_connection: The value model rewards predicted dwell, click-dwell and sharing (dwell, cont_click_dwell_time, share_via_copy_link weights). Long-form articles plausibly raise those predictions; the repo does not contain an article-specific boost.
alternatives: ["Article topics may simply be the account's strongest topics", 'X may surface Articles through surfaces outside the For You ranking studied here', 'Articles are often promoted harder (pinned, quoted by co-founders/peers)']
impact: Largest observed lever: shifting mix toward the best format changes the median outcome, not just outliers.
recommendation: Make X Articles (with a strong native preview post) the anchor format, and turn short standalone posts into either article teasers or replies.
validation: A/B over 4 weeks: alternate article vs non-article on matched topics; compare median views per format.
success_criteria: Article posts keep >= the current ratio vs other formats while posting volume is held constant.

observation: Median views on authored posts trend at 0.83x per 30 days (90% CI 0.78–0.88, n=301); monthly medians went from 5663 (2026-04) to 2924 (2026-10).
algo_connection: Out-of-network retrieval is driven by viewers' recent engagement histories (Phoenix two-tower, SimClusters seeds). A sustained decline is consistent with fewer viewers having recently engaged with the account, but the repository cannot attribute it.
alternatives: ['Change in content mix (fewer X Articles or long tutorials in recent months)', 'Seasonality / audience attention (summer vs autumn)', 'Platform-wide changes in view counting or feed composition (weights changed in Sept–Oct; see parameter history)', "Recent posts' views still accruing despite the 72h maturity filter"]
impact: Determines whether the priority is recovering lost distribution or growing from a stable base.
recommendation: Track weekly median views for each format separately so a format-mix shift is not mistaken for a reach decline; re-run after 4 weeks of monitoring.
validation: Format-stratified weekly medians from continuous monitoring; check the trend within X Articles only.
success_criteria: Weekly authored median views stop declining for 4 consecutive weeks (format-adjusted).

observation: Replies per 1,000 views: 0.98 vs peer median 1.81 (0.54x). Likes per 1,000 views: 5.71 vs 9.86. Bookmarks per 1,000 views: 8.76 vs 2.76.
algo_connection: Published defaults weight a viewer's predicted reply probability at 5.0 versus 0.66 for a like; for original posts from an author the viewer mutually follows, the reply weight is raised by a further 15.0. Weights multiply the model's predicted probabilities per viewer, not raw counts, so observed reply rates are only an outcome proxy for what the model predicts.
alternatives: ['Audience composition differs from peers (more lurkers / buyers who do not reply)', 'Lead-magnet CTAs convert replies into keyword comments counted elsewhere', 'Peer accounts differ in size; per-view rates partly normalise this but not fully']
impact: Conversation is the most heavily weighted positive action family; raising it is the most algorithm-aligned lever available from content alone.
recommendation: End posts with a specific, answerable prompt tied to the post's claim; reply to early commenters within the first hour to deepen threads.
validation: Compare replies per 1k views on posts with vs without a specific closing prompt over 4 weeks.
success_criteria: Median replies per 1k views on authored posts moves toward the peer median.

issue: Commenting is low-depth and concentrated on a small circle
observation: 88 conversational comments in the window; 33% are substantive and 39% are generic, repetitive or humour. The top 5 accounts receive 49% of comments; median exposure is 58.5 views per comment.
algo_connection: In the published For You pipeline, out-of-network replies are filtered out by default and in-network replies receive the 0.75 out-of-network-style rescore, so a comment is seen mainly inside the parent conversation, not distributed in feeds. Comments can still build mutual-follow relationships, and the reply weight is raised for original posts from mutually-followed authors. The repo has no 'comment boost' for the commenter's own posts.
alternatives: ['Comments within a founder circle may serve partnership/relationship goals rather than reach', 'Parent-post context (unavailable for most replies) may make short replies more relevant than they look']
impact: Comment exposure is small per reply; quality matters more than volume for building recognition.
recommendation: Replace generic agreement with 2-3 sentence expert additions on larger in-niche accounts' posts within their first hour; keep relationship comments but stop emoji/one-word replies.
validation: Track median views and reply-backs per comment for 'expert addition' comments vs the current mix.
success_criteria: Substantive share > 60% and median views per comment above current median.

observation: The top two topics account for 53% of authored posts. Topics associated with higher reach: LinkedIn & social selling 1.4x.
algo_connection: SimClusters and Phoenix retrieval match posts to viewers whose recent engagement resembles the post. Consistent topics make it more likely the right viewers already have related engagement history; the repo exposes no per-account topic score.
alternatives: ['Topic effects overlap with format (tutorial topics are more often articles)', 'Off-core posts may be personal/timely and judged on other goals']
impact: Concentrating on the strongest clusters improves the median post without adding volume.
recommendation: Prioritise the higher-reach topics listed; reduce off-core posts or move them to replies.
validation: Re-run the topic comparison after 6 weeks with the regression (format + month controls).
success_criteria: Share of authored posts in the higher-reach topics rises with no fall in their median.

issue: Several authored posts on the same day
observation: Third-or-later authored posts on the same day reach a median 0.6x of baseline (n=52) versus 0.94x for the first post of the day (n=141).
algo_connection: vm-ranker applies an author-diversity multiplier within each viewer's ranked feed: a repeat author's later candidates are multiplied by (1 - floor) * decay^k + floor with AuthorDiversityDecay 0.5 and AuthorDiversityFloor 0.25. Several fresh posts compete for the same viewer slots. This is per viewer request, so it is a plausible mechanism, not a measured penalty on this account.
alternatives: ['Later posts of the day may be lower-effort or reactive', 'Time-of-day differences (later posts land outside peak hours)', 'Small sample for 3rd+ posts']
impact: Spacing posts is a free change; if the association is real, it recovers reach on the weakest third of posts.
recommendation: Cap authored posts at 2 per day, at least 6 hours apart; move extra content into replies, threads, or the next day.
validation: 2-week alternating schedule (stacked vs spaced days) with the same formats; compare vs-baseline medians.
success_criteria: 3rd+-post days disappear without lowering weekly total views.

observation: The top 5% of authored posts produced 47% of authored views; the single top post 13%. 28% of posts land below half the trailing baseline and 25% above twice it.
algo_connection: Out-of-network discovery starts small (cold-start pool for posts with few likes/views; retrieval-index admission triggered by likes) and only some posts escape it. Heavy-tailed outcomes are expected from this design.
alternatives: ['Viral posts may be driven by external resharing (large accounts, newsletters)']
impact: Averages mislead: judge experiments on medians and share-above-baseline, not totals.
recommendation: Reverse-engineer the top posts' structure into a repeatable template; judge tests on medians.
validation: Share of posts above 2x baseline per month.
success_criteria: Share above 2x baseline rises without lowering the median.

observation: Opening/structure patterns with clear differences: Opening hook type = how_to: 1.7x (n=101); Narrative structure = promotion: 2.68x (n=18); Narrative structure = tutorial: 1.36x (n=113); Educational value (0-3) = 2.0: 1.68x (n=138); Opening hook type = contrarian: 0.67x (n=29); Educational value (0-3) = 0.0: 0.59x (n=43); Educational value (0-3) = 3.0: 0.65x (n=85).
algo_connection: Dwell and click-dwell predictions are weighted positively and 'not_dwelled' negatively in published defaults; an opening that earns an expand plausibly raises those predictions.
alternatives: ['Hook type correlates with format and topic', 'Labels are model judgements and can be noisy']
impact: Hooks are cheap to change and testable post-by-post.
recommendation: Lead with the concrete outcome or how-to promise; avoid opinion-only or vague observational openers.
validation: Paired test: same topic, two hook styles on different days; compare vs-baseline ratios.
success_criteria: Hook-type gap persists in a controlled 4-week test.

observation: 1140 template replies ('Sent', 'Here you go: <link>') to 1060 distinct accounts, about 44.6 per week. These are fulfilment of comment-for-resource CTAs, inferred from their template text.
algo_connection: A published botmaker rule clusters replies with duplicate text and applies a COPYPASTA_SPAM label (skipping high-PageRank and grey-verified users), and the Grox reply_spam flow can label risky replies. Whether these clients' identical 'Sent' replies are labelled, and what any label does to reach, is not observable and partly withheld; this is a risk to monitor, not an observed penalty.
alternatives: ['Keyword-CTA posts generate many replies, which is itself a strong positive signal', 'Templated fulfilment is normal for lead magnets and widely used by peers']
impact: Mainly risk management and time cost; also inflates 'reply' counts so commenting looks larger than it is.
recommendation: Keep lead magnets but vary fulfilment (short personalised line + resource), or deliver via one pinned reply / DM automation instead of hundreds of identical public replies.
validation: Compare authored-post reach in weeks with vs without mass fulfilment replies (matched formats).
success_criteria: No drop in lead-magnet conversions with < 25% of current identical public replies.

observation: Among non-article authored posts, posts containing a t.co URL (external link or media) reach 1.31x the median of those without (n=81 vs 115).
algo_connection: The published ranking code contains no link penalty: open_link carries a small positive weight. has_url is computed only for an experimental debias payload that is off by default. Media and external links cannot be separated in this data.
alternatives: ['t.co URLs include attached media, which may help', 'Link posts are often promotional']
impact: Determines whether link placement should change; the repository gives no reason to expect a penalty.
recommendation: Do not restructure content around a link penalty; if testing, put the link in a self-reply on half of link posts and compare.
validation: Randomised link-in-post vs link-in-reply on comparable posts for 4 weeks.

observation: 0 of 301 mature authored posts have fewer than 100 views; reach is continuous with the account's normal range. No public signal indicates a visibility restriction; this audit cannot observe X's visibility-filtering decisions.
algo_connection: Visibility filtering (Allow/Notice/Interstitial/Drop) and account-quality systems exist in the repository, but their per-account outputs are not public.
alternatives: ['Any decline is better explained by format/topic mix and the trend analysis']
impact: No action warranted on current evidence; claims of suppression would be speculation.
recommendation: Do not act on shadowban theories; monitor for abrupt step-changes (>50% week-on-week drop across all formats) as the trigger to investigate.
validation: Monitoring alert on control limits (rolling median ± 3 MAD) across formats.
